notes.meaning: Athaliah was the mother of King Ahaziah of Judah. When her son was killed, she seized the throne by murdering all the royal heirs she could find. In her fierce ambition, she nearly wiped out the family line of David that God had promised to preserve.

Jehosheba, the king's sister and the wife of the high priest, secretly rescued the baby Joash before he could be killed. She hid him and his nurse in a palace storage room used for keeping bedding. By her brave action, God protected the one surviving heir of David's royal line.

The young boy Joash was hidden safely in the temple living quarters for six years. Meanwhile, Athaliah ruled over Judah as an unlawful queen. During these quiet years, God preserved the royal seed out of public sight.

In the seventh year of Athaliah's reign, the high priest Jehoiada sent for the commanders and the palace guards to meet him at the temple. He made them take a solemn oath of loyalty before the Lord. Then he showed them the young prince who had been kept in hiding.

Jehoiada arranged the guards on the Sabbath, when one group of temple guards was going on duty and another was finishing. He ordered three divisions to guard the entrances and watch toward the palace so no enemy could break into the temple. The other two divisions were stationed inside the house of the Lord to keep constant guard over the young king.

Jehoiada told the guards to keep their weapons ready and surround the young king on every side. Anyone who tried to break through the lines was to be put to death immediately. The guards were ordered to stay close to Joash wherever he moved.

The commanders obeyed every order given by Jehoiada the priest. They assembled their men, both those who were coming on duty for the Sabbath and those who were going off duty. Together they reported to the high priest at the temple.

Jehoiada handed out the spears and shields that King David had dedicated and stored in the temple. The commanders had arrived unarmed so they would not attract suspicion. David's own weapons were now placed in their hands to help restore David's rightful heir to the throne.

The armed guards formed a protective wall across the temple court, from the south side to the north. They stood by the altar of sacrifice and the main temple building. In this way, they secured the whole area where the young king would be presented.

Jehoiada brought out Joash, placed the crown on his head, and handed him the Testimony, which was God's written law. The priests poured oil on him to show he was chosen by God to rule. The people clapped their hands with joy and shouted for the king's long life.

Athaliah heard the noise of the guards and the loud shouting of the crowd. She hurried into the temple courts to find out what was happening. She entered without an escort, walking directly into the trap that was waiting for her.

Athaliah saw the young king standing on the royal platform by the pillar, surrounded by commanders and trumpeters while the people rejoiced. Seeing her power slip away, she tore her clothes in terror and rage. She screamed that this was treason, even though she was the unlawful ruler who had seized power by violence.

Jehoiada ordered the army officers to march Athaliah out of the temple between ranks of armed men. He commanded that anyone who tried to follow or defend her must be killed on the spot. He insisted that she must not be executed inside the temple, so God's sacred house would not be stained with blood.

The guards seized Athaliah and escorted her out toward the palace grounds. When she reached the gate where horses entered the king's stables, they put her to death. Her wicked reign came to an end right outside the royal house she had stolen.

Jehoiada made a covenant—a sacred agreement—between the Lord, the king, and the people, pledging that they would live as God's faithful followers. He also made a covenant between the king and the people. Under this pact, the king agreed to govern by God's law, and the people promised loyal obedience to their ruler.

The people went straight to the temple of the false god Baal and tore it down. They smashed its altars and pagan images to pieces, and they executed Mattan, the priest of Baal, right in front of those altars. Then Jehoiada appointed officers to guard the Lord's house and make sure true worship was faithfully restored.

other.label: Modern scholarship
other.view: Some scholars note that the biblical text does not explicitly state that Athaliah worshipped Baal or built this temple, suggesting the conflict may have been more political than religious.

notes.meaning: Jehoiada, the commanders, the guards, and all the people escorted the young king from the temple to the royal palace. They entered the palace through the Gate of the Guards. Joash was then seated upon the royal throne, returning David's dynasty to its rightful place.

All the people of the land celebrated with great joy, and Jerusalem was peaceful and quiet. The tyrant Athaliah had been killed by the sword near the palace, and none of her supporters rose up to fight. True peace returned to the city when the rightful king took the throne.

Joash was only seven years old when he became king of Judah. Even though he was just a child, he was guided by a wise, godly high priest and protected by the Lord. His coronation proved that God had kept His ancient promise to David's family.
